race.name: GFNY Puerto Rico
race.tagline: A fast 115-kilometer Caribbean race from Ponce, with coastal wind and one gradual fifteen-kilometer climb.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.description: March in southern Puerto Rico is warm, sunny, and humid. Coastal wind offers some cooling but also creates tactical crosswind exposure on the fastest parts of the course.
challenges: High fluid demand at race speed

terrain.primary: Fast coastal roads with one gradual inland climb
terrain.surface: Paved highways and rural roads across Puerto Rico's southern coastal plain.
features: Fast opening roads through Ponce and along PR-1
A long exposed coastal approach through Santa Isabel and Salinas
A 15-kilometer gradual climb from sea level
A 7.5-kilometer descent before the coastal return

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Established GFNY organization, accessible logistics, and a fast competitive course score well. Modest climbing and limited global prestige cap the grade.

key_climbs: Fast opening roads through Ponce and along PR-1
A long exposed coastal approach through Santa Isabel and Salinas
A 15-kilometer gradual climb from sea level
A 7.5-kilometer descent before the coastal return
climb_profile.profile_type: Fast coastal roads with one gradual inland climb
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The 15-kilometer climb from sea level, whose final four kilometers become the course's clearest selection point.

course_description.character: The long race starts and finishes at the Ponce Hilton, uses broad and fast roads across the southern coastal plain, and introduces its decisive terrain with a gradual 15-kilometer climb beginning around kilometer 40. The elevation is modest, but Caribbean heat, wind, and high group speed keep the race demanding.
course_description.signature_challenge: The 15-kilometer climb from sea level, whose final four kilometers become the course's clearest selection point.

logistics.airport: Mercedita International Airport (PSE) is closest; Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport (SJU) has the broadest service and is roughly 90 minutes from Ponce.
logistics.lodging_strategy: The Ponce Hilton is race headquarters. Central Ponce offers additional hotels, but confirm bike storage and race-morning access.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: Ponce has plentiful rice, plantain, seafood, and criollo options. Keep the pre-race meal simple and begin hydration before arriving in the heat.

history.origin_story: GFNY brought its competitive gran fondo format to Puerto Rico in 2022 and later moved the event to Ponce, where the southern-coast course became faster and more accessible.
notable_moments: 2024: The race moves to a mountainous Ponce course
history.reputation: A fast Caribbean GFNY backed by an established local field and the series' standard competitive rules.

biased_opinion.summary: The long race starts and finishes at the Ponce Hilton, uses broad and fast roads across the southern coastal plain, and introduces its decisive terrain with a gradual 15-kilometer climb beginning around kilometer 40. The elevation is modest, but Caribbean heat, wind, and high group speed keep the race demanding.
weaknesses: Much of the course is exposed highway
The route lacks a major signature mountain
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A legitimate fast-road GFNY where heat management and peloton skill matter more than climbing pedigree.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fast 115-kilometer Caribbean race from Ponce, with coastal wind and one gradual fifteen-kilometer climb.
final_verdict.should_you_race: A legitimate fast-road GFNY where heat management and peloton skill matter more than climbing pedigree.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY República Dominicana for another Caribbean GFNY, or GFNY Miami for an even flatter wind-driven race.
